{{Short description|Integer where the average of its positive divisors is also an integer}}
[[File:Arithmetic number Cuisenaire rods 6.png|thumb|Demonstration, with [[Cuisenaire rods]], of the arithmetic nature of the number 6]]

In [[number theory]], an '''arithmetic number''' is an [[integer]] for which the [[arithmetic mean|average]] of its [[positive number|positive]] [[divisor]]s is also an integer.  For instance, 6 is an arithmetic number because the average of its divisors is
:<math>\frac{1+2+3+6}{4}=3,</math>
which is also an integer. However, 2 is not an arithmetic number because its only divisors are 1 and 2, and their average 3/2 is not an integer.

The first numbers in the [[integer sequence|sequence]] of arithmetic numbers are
:1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11, 13, 14, 15, 17, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 27, 29, 30, 31, 33, 35, 37, 38, 39, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 49, ... {{OEIS|id=A003601}}.

The [[arithmetic mean]]s of the divisors of arithmetic numbers are listed at {{OEIS link|id=A102187}}.

==Density==
It is known that the [[natural density]] of such numbers is 1:<ref name=G76>Guy (2004) p.76</ref> indeed, the proportion of numbers less than ''X'' which are not arithmetic is [[Asymptotic analysis|asymptotically]]<ref name=BEPS>{{cite book | zbl=0478.10027 | last1=Bateman | first1=Paul T. | author1-link=Paul T. Bateman | last2=Erdős | first2=Paul | author2-link=Paul Erdős | last3=Pomerance | first3=Carl | author3-link=Carl Pomerance | last4=Straus | first4=E.G. | author4-link=Ernst G. Straus | chapter=The arithmetic mean of the divisors of an integer| title=Analytic number theory, Proc. Conf., Temple Univ., 1980 | editor-first=M.I. | editor-last=Knopp | editor-link=Marvin Knopp | series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics | volume=899 | pages=197–220 | year=1981 | publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] | url = https://www.math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/PDF/31.pdf}}</ref>

:<math>\exp\left( { -c \sqrt{\log\log X} } \,\right)</math>

where ''c'' = 2{{radic|log 2}} + o(1).

A number ''N'' is arithmetic if the [[number of divisors]] ''d''(''N''{{hairsp}}) divides the [[Sum-of-divisors function|sum of divisors]] σ(''N''{{hairsp}}).  It is known that the [[natural density|density]] of integers ''N'' obeying the stronger condition that ''d''(''N''{{hairsp}})<sup>2</sup> divides σ(''N''{{hairsp}}) is 1/2.<ref name=G76/><ref name=BEPS/>
